# CLI reference

Resource, cache and output directories are described in [Install & resources](install.md).

## Subcommands and exit codes

Exit codes are `0` for success, `1` for a failure the command reports as `error: <sentence>`
on stderr, and `64` for a usage error. The table lists, per subcommand, which conditions give
which code.

| Invocation | Exit codes |
| --- | --- |
| `genefox` (no arguments), `genefox help`, `--help`, `-h` | 0: prints usage to stdout. |
| `genefox <unknown>` | 64: `unknown command: <name>`, then usage, on stderr. |
| `genefox catalog [--json]` | 0. |
| `genefox validate <recipe.json>` | 0 on success; 64 for a missing or extra argument; 1 when the file is missing or invalid. |
| `genefox render …` | 0 on success; 64 for a usage error; 1 for other failures. |
| `genefox fetch <url> …` | 0 on success; 64 for a usage error or a bad `-m`; 1 for a transport or decompression error. |
| `genefox report export …` | 0 on success; 1 for every failure, **including argument errors**. |
| `genefox doctor [--resources <dir>] [--output-dir <dir>]` | 0 when healthy; 1 if a required check fails; 64 for a usage error. Diagnostics go to stdout. |
| `genefox curated validate <dir> [--json]` | 0 when the dataset package is valid; 1 when it has issues (printed as `file:line:column: message [code]`, or as the JSON report with `--json`); 1 for a usage error. |
| `genefox curated dose <view> <package-dir> [flags]` | The `genefox run dose_response` result: 0 on success; 1 when refused (no live Dose-Response grant, an unknown name, a package that fails its pins, a path outside the read root); 64 for a usage error. See the [MCP server guide](mcp.md#entitlements-genefox-pro). |
| `genefox update [--check] [--version X.Y.Z]` | 0 when updated, already current, or (with `--check`) reported; 1 when it refuses or a check fails; 64 for a usage error. |
| `genefox tools` | 0; 64 if any argument is given. |
| `genefox mcp [options]` | 64 for an option error; 0 when stdin reaches EOF and every in-flight call has answered; 0 when writing to stdout fails because the client has gone. |
| `genefox helper <command>` | The account helper's own exit codes: 2 for its usage. On macOS the command forwards to the signed helper binary, so its exit codes are the helper's; 1 when the helper is missing or its signature does not verify. |

`render` treats a missing recipe, a second positional argument, an unrecognised option, or
`--r-script` without `--storage-dir` as usage errors (64). Its `--r-script` combined with
`--size` exits 1.

### `genefox catalog [--json]`

Prints the operation catalogue (the same list `list_operations` returns): id, display name,
summary and data scope. `--json` prints the same records as sorted, pretty-printed JSON, in
the same form the MCP `list_operations` tool returns.

### `genefox validate <recipe.json>`

Decodes a recipe store file (the JSON file GeneFox writes when you save recipes),
validates every recipe and resolves its operation. It prints one line per recipe:
`validated: <name> — dataset <catalog>/<id>, operation <id>`. Entries this build cannot read
are counted and reported, never silently dropped. The CLI does not enforce the store's
envelope-level policy (format id, version, caps). The legacy MCP tool `validate_recipe` gives
the same verdict.

### `genefox render <recipe.json> [options]`

Replays the **first** recipe in the file and writes a PNG, or with `--r-script`, R source.

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--storage-dir <dir>` | A local imported-dataset store. Required for imported recipes and for `--r-script`. |
| `--size <preset>` | `single_column`, `one_and_a_half_column`, `double_column`, `slide` or `poster`. Without it, a public recipe uses its recorded figure size, or `double_column` if it has none, and an imported recipe uses `double_column`. Rejected with `--r-script`. |
| `--r-script` | Emit the exact-input R script for an imported heatmap, signature or differential-expression recipe, instead of a PNG. |
| `-o <file>` | Write to this file and print `wrote N bytes PNG` (or `… R source`). Without `-o`, the bytes go to stdout. Overwrites. |

Imported recipes replay from the verified local store. Public-dataset recipes replay through
the MCP tools' shared runners (network access needed) into a private temporary directory,
which is removed afterwards. They also need resources and a font that passes its pin. A
destination with no verifiable PNG replay refuses. The size is capped at 8,192 px per side
and 16,000,000 px in total.

### `genefox fetch <url> [-o <file>] [-z] [-m <bytes>]`

Fetches a URL through the CLI's **unrestricted** transport (the MCP server's host allowlist
does not apply here) and prints the body, or writes it with `-o` (overwrites). `-z`
gunzips the response. `-m` is the maximum response size in bytes: default 50,000,000,
allowed range 1 to 100,663,296. A value outside
that range exits 64.

### `genefox report export <file> [options]`

Reads a saved GeneFox v1/v2 report, renders it through the PDF assembly
the apps use, and writes it create-only to the output directory. It then prints
`wrote N bytes PDF to <path>`.

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--format pdf` | The only format accepted. |
| `--output-dir <dir>` | Output directory (see [Output files](install.md#output-files)); or `GENEFOX_OUTPUT_DIR`. |
| `--resources <dir>` | Authoritative report assets; or `GENEFOX_RESOURCES`, then install-prefix/app-bundle discovery. Uses bundled report assets when no scientific root is selected. |
| `--generated-at <ISO8601>` | Fixed document timestamp with a time zone (years 0001–9999), for reproducible bytes. |
| `--without-methods` | Omit the auto-generated Methods pages. |

The report path must be a regular file, not a symbolic link, and fit this process's
memory-derived size limit. Unreadable figures, invalid figure sizes, or tables over the
budget refuse with no partial PDF written.

### `genefox curated validate <dir> [--json]`

Checks a curated dataset package (manifest, columns dictionary, expression matrices and tables). Nothing is fetched and nothing is written.

### `genefox curated dose <view> <package-dir> [flags]`

GeneFox Pro's dose-response analyses on an assembled curated package (`resource.json`, `tables/<id>.tsv.gz`, `metadata.tsv`), the same calls the app's dose panes make. Views: `curve` (also `table`: one compound's IC50 and AUC per line, refit and published side by side, and a line's curve), `by_group`, `waterfall`, `volcano`, `mechanism`, `heatmap` (the `--top` most informative compounds, `--rank variation|strength`, x the lines for the measure: `--measure log10_ic50 --ic50 absolute|relative`, `auc` or `amax`; lines grouped by `--column`, and `--level <value>` (repeatable) draws the lines with any of those values, as one group, against all other lines; `--scale z_score` standardizes per compound; a hatched cell is not reached, gray is not tested; `--style dots` draws the same matrix as dots, colour log10 IC50 and size Amax in % effect, a hollow dot a fitted-asymptote Amax, an outlined dot not reached), `biomarkers` (one compound against every gene: `--test expression` Spearman or `--test mutation` Wilcoxon mutant vs wild-type, BH across the family, n per test, at least 6 lines or 3 per group; `--direction gene --gene G` for one gene against every compound; published values by default), `single_dose_ranked`, `single_dose_by_group`, `single_dose_volcano`, `single_dose_bridge`. Every grouping view groups by `--column`, or by a gene: `--group-by expression --gene G [--split median|tertiles]` or `--group-by mutation --gene G` (the package's variant table), or by `stratify_derived` (an annotation column or `expression:G`). The package's `matrix.gfxm` supplies expression. Flags: `--compound`, `--line`, `--column`, `--control`, `--group-1`, `--group-2`, `--measure auc|log10_ic50|amax`, `--source refit|published` (volcano, mechanism and heatmap default to published when the package has it), `--ic50 absolute|relative`, `--fdr`, `--plot strip|box`, `--scale z_score|median|value`, `--top`, `--rank`, `--style cells|dots`, `--level`, `--table`, `--limit`, `--figure true|false`, `--size`, `--format png|svg|tiff|pdf`, `--csv`, `--output-dir`. The result is JSON: the pane's table, the Methods sentence with each table's own credit, the dose method hints, and the figure and CSV paths. The package directory is also the read root for the call. Without a live Dose-Response grant the tool is not offered and the command exits 1 (this headless build links no account, so it fails closed everywhere today).

### `genefox update [--check] [--version X.Y.Z]`

`genefox update` updates an install made by the GeneFox installer in place: it makes the installer's checks (GeneFox's
minisign signature, a trusted comment naming `genefox-cli` and the exact version, the
archive's SHA-256), runs the new binary, then swaps it in. `genefox update --check` only
reports; `genefox update --version X.Y.Z` installs that version, which is the only way to go
back to an older one. It refuses a Homebrew or conda install, the copy inside GeneFox.app and a
folder you cannot write, and prints the command to use instead. On Windows the running
`genefox.exe` is renamed aside and removed by the next update.

Once a day, in a terminal, genefox prints a one-line notice on stderr when a newer release
exists. The check runs in the background with a 3-second limit and never delays or fails a
command. It is never shown for `genefox mcp`, when stdout or stderr is not a terminal, in CI
(`CI` set), or with `GENEFOX_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1`.

### `genefox doctor [--resources <dir>] [--output-dir <dir>]`

Runs offline startup checks and prints one line per check: the scientific resource inventory
and Ensembl reference (found/missing and path), bundled report marks and fonts (found/missing
and path), the figure font's SHA-256 pin, an actual create-only write under the output root,
the digest/inflate/transport seams and remaining required seams,
an informational line of the should/pro/optional seams this host leaves uninstalled (never a
failure), and the sorted MCP fetch allowlist. The write probe is removed afterwards. `genefox fetch` remains unrestricted.

For source builds, a binary under the checkout's `.build` folder finds the app's scientific resources directory itself; `--resources`
(or `GENEFOX_RESOURCES`) still wins. Explicit resources are authoritative for report assets too. `--output-dir` wins
over `GENEFOX_OUTPUT_DIR`, then defaults to `<system temp>/genefox-mcp`; a missing output
directory is created under the usual output policy. A missing or corrupt resource, font-pin
mismatch, failed write, or missing required seam exits **1**; all checks passing exits **0**.
A malformed option exits **64**. Missing-resource diagnostics name the manifest, reference
or report asset that failed.

### `genefox tools`

Prints the MCP tool catalogue as a markdown table: every tool this build registers, its
access class (free, Pro or legacy) and its deadline. The [tool catalogue](tools.md) is generated from this output.

### `genefox mcp [options]`

Serves MCP over stdio. Requests go in on stdin and responses come out on stdout; logs go to
stderr. File descriptor 1 is pointed at stderr so that a stray `print` cannot
corrupt the protocol stream.

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--resources <dir>` | Scientific resources (see the [install guide](install.md#scientific-resources-resources-dir-genefox_resources)); or `GENEFOX_RESOURCES`, then resolved install prefix, then app bundle. |
| `--cache-dir <dir>` | Download cache; or `GENEFOX_CACHE_DIR`. Default: the native caches directory plus `GeneFoxCLI` (`~/Library/Caches/GeneFoxCLI`, or `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/GeneFoxCLI` on Linux). Available on every subcommand. |
| `--output-dir <dir>` | Where figures, CSVs, recipes and HTML are written; or `GENEFOX_OUTPUT_DIR`. Default `<system temp>/genefox-mcp`. |
| `--enable-legacy-tools` | Also list `report_export_pdf`, `report_export_html`, `validate_recipe`, `fetch_url` and `render_recipe`. These take local paths or URLs. |
| `--imported-store <dir>` | The local imported-dataset store that the legacy `render_recipe` may read for imported recipes. Only this flag names it; no tool argument can. |
| `--allow-root <dir>` | An extra local read root for the legacy `validate_recipe`/`render_recipe` paths, repeatable; or `GENEFOX_MCP_ALLOWED_ROOTS` (path-separated). The output directory and the imported store are always roots; a model-named path outside every root is refused. |
| `--warm <list>` | Comma-separated background prefetch: `toil`, `pancan`, or project ids the tools accept (for example `TCGA-BRCA`). Unknown tokens are logged and skipped. Skipped entirely without resources. |
| `--call-timeout <seconds>` | One deadline, from 1 to 3600 seconds, for every call, replacing each tool's own. |
| `--max-concurrent-calls <n>` | How many `tools/call`s run at once, from 1 to 64 (default: half the processors, at least 2 and at most 4). Up to 16 more queue; beyond that a call answers `rate_limited` (retryable). |

A flag that takes a value refuses a following argument that starts with `--`. Every option
error exits 64 and prints the usage line on stderr.

#### Showing only some groups: `keep_groups`

`geo_series_expression`, `geo_gene_correlation`, `tcga_expression`, `geo_sample_pca`,
`tcga_sample_pca` and `reference_ccle_expression` take `keep_groups`: the levels of the figure's
factor to show (the grouping, or a scatter's colour; `tcga_expression` takes
`keep_color_groups` for its correlation scatter). Levels are matched exactly, as R's `%in%`
matches them, and dropped levels are gone, as `droplevels` drops them: r, r², n, the group
test and its degrees of freedom are recomputed on the retained samples (a PCA is re-solved on
them). A level the data no longer has is refused, never ignored. The result's `data.subset`
carries the engine's sentence ("Showing k of m <factor> groups: ...; statistics recomputed on
the n retained samples."), which the recipe and HTML export also carry; GEO level names go
under `untrusted_*`. No deep link is returned for a filtered figure, since a link cannot
record the filter; the recipe does.
